=== Page 1 ===
FICTIONAL SAMPLE POLICY - FOR SOFTWARE TESTING ONLY. NOT A REAL COVERAGE POLICY.

Sample Coverage Policy SAMPLE-TKA-001
Total Knee Arthroplasty (Total Knee Replacement)
Applies to CPT 27447 (Arthroplasty, knee, condyle and plateau; medial and lateral compartments)
Fictional Example Health Plan - Effective date: January 1, 2026

Purpose
This sample policy describes when a total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is considered reasonable
and necessary. It was written for a demonstration of decision-support software and must not
be used for real coverage decisions.

Background
Total knee arthroplasty relieves pain and restores function for patients with end-stage
knee arthritis. Because it is a major operation with real risks, it is reserved for patients
with advanced joint disease that limits daily life and who have not improved with non-surgical
care, unless the joint is so badly damaged that non-surgical care cannot help.

=== Page 2 ===
Coverage Indications

Section A - Disease severity (ALL of the following must be met)

A1. Imaging evidence of advanced arthritis of the knee: plain radiographs (X-rays) showing
Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4 changes, or severe joint space narrowing with osteophytes,
subchondral sclerosis, or bone-on-bone contact.

A2. Moderate to severe knee pain with functional limitation that interferes with activities
of daily living, such as walking, climbing stairs, standing, or sleeping.

Section B - Non-surgical care (at least ONE of the following must be met)

B1. Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment. Non-surgical treatment includes
physical therapy or a supervised exercise program, NSAIDs or other analgesics, intra-articular
corticosteroid injections, weight loss when appropriate, and assistive devices or bracing.
The types and duration of treatment must be documented.

B2. Advanced joint destruction where non-surgical treatment would not be expected to help:
avascular necrosis of the femoral condyle or tibial plateau, collapse of the joint surface,
or severe fixed deformity.

=== Page 3 ===
Limitations
Total knee arthroplasty is not covered when there is an active infection in the knee or
elsewhere in the body.

Coding Information - ICD-10-CM codes that support medical necessity
M17.0   Bilateral primary osteoarthritis of knee
M17.11  Unilateral primary osteoarthritis, right knee
M17.12  Unilateral primary osteoarthritis, left knee
M17.31  Unilateral post-traumatic osteoarthritis, right knee
M17.32  Unilateral post-traumatic osteoarthritis, left knee
M87.051 Idiopathic aseptic necrosis of right femur

Documentation Requirements
The medical record must include the imaging report, a description of pain and functional
limitation, and the non-surgical treatments tried with their duration.
